notes: Full description: pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs parse_der_length() at lines 291-308. The function handles 'long-form' DER lengths up to 4 bytes: 'if n_bytes == 0 || n_bytes > 4 || rest.len() < n_bytes { return None; }'. However, a legitimate RSA key's DER encoding uses standard short-form or long-form lengths. The 4-byte limit means max parseable content is ~4 GiB, but the key byte limit is that RSA keys are rarely > 16384 bits = 2048 bytes. The integer overflow protection uses checked_shl(8) and checked_add(b as usize), which is correct. HOWEVER: the comment says 'n_bytes > 4' rejects > 4-byte lengths, but the RSAPublicKey for very large (hypothetical) keys could theoretically have a modulus length needing > 2 bytes of DER length encoding. For a 2048-byte modulus, DER length is 0x82 0x08 0x00 (3 bytes for 2048). 4 bytes of DER length encoding allows up to 4 GiB content, which is sufficient for any realistic RSA key. The checked arithmetic protects against overflow. Actually this is fine — no bug here. Closing this finding as not a real issue. Mark as P4 (opinion — the code is correct).
title: FINDING (P4/opinion): parse_der_length 4-byte limit - not a bug
